title: Waldorf Salad
subtitle: Classic American salad of apple, celery, walnuts, and mayonnaise
excerpt: The original Waldorf Hotel salad of crisp apple, celery, and walnuts dressed in lightly lemoned mayonnaise. A simple, satisfying salad that works as a starter or a light lunch.

recipe.sourceNotes: The Waldorf Salad was created in 1893 by Oscar Tschirky, the maitre d' of the Waldorf Hotel in New York (later the Waldorf-Astoria). The original version contained only three ingredients: apple, celery, and mayonnaise. Walnuts were added in the early twentieth century and have been part of the standard recipe ever since. In Britain the salad became widely known through the 1970s and 1980s and was for a period a staple of hotel dining and buffet tables; it was memorably lampooned in a 1979 Fawlty Towers episode in which Basil Fawlty cannot source the walnuts. The salad's reputation was rehabilitated in the 1990s and 2000s. Serve on a bed of cos or romaine lettuce.

content.text: Toss the cut apple immediately in lemon juice to prevent browning. The walnuts can be lightly toasted in a dry pan for 3 minutes for a deeper flavour, though the original uses raw walnuts. Do not dress the salad more than 30 minutes before serving or the celery will soften and the apple will weep. A small amount of natural yoghurt can replace some of the mayonnaise for a lighter result.

items.preparation: Cox or Braeburn, cored and diced; tossed in lemon juice

content.text: Toss the diced apple with half the lemon juice immediately to prevent browning.
Mix together the mayonnaise, remaining lemon juice, and salt. Taste: it should be sharp and creamy.
Combine the apple, celery, and walnuts. Pour over the dressing and toss to coat. Serve on a bed of lettuce leaves. Eat within 30 minutes of dressing.
